title: White Nights

vibeProfile.oneLine: Four luminous nights, a lonely dreamer, and a love that was never his to keep.

summary: A lonely young dreamer wanders the empty summer streets of St Petersburg during its luminous white nights, and over four evenings falls into conversation, then something like love, with a young woman named Nastenka who is waiting for someone else. Almost nothing happens, and yet it aches. Dostoevsky's early novella is a small, luminous study of the kind of person who lives more fully in his imagination than his life, and of the tenderness and heartbreak of a connection that was never quite his to keep.
whyReadIt: The most tender thing Dostoevsky ever wrote, and the gentlest way into him. A short, glowing ache of a book about loneliness and one brief, impossible closeness.

funFacts.text: Its title refers to the real phenomenon of St Petersburg's 'white nights', when the sun barely sets in midsummer.
